body.statement: In a canonical latent-variable LiNGAM with unknown graph, let \(u\) and \(v\) be observed variables and let \(\operatorname{de}_o(a)\) be the observed descendants of a node \(a\). The total effect of \(u\) on \(v\) is generically identifiable if and only if there is no latent node \(h\) such that \(\operatorname{de}_o(u)=\operatorname{de}_o(h)\) and \(v\in\operatorname{de}^{G\setminus u}_o(h)\), where \(G\setminus u\) deletes all arrows into \(u\).

source.verbatim_statement: Consider any two observed variables i and j. The total causal effect of j on i is generically identifiable without knowledge of the graph if and only if there is no l in L such that de_o(j) = de_o(l), and i is in the observed descendants of l in the graph obtained from G by removing all edges pointing to j.
